「締太鼓」（shime-daiko）一詞源自較長的詞彙「附締太鼓」（tsukes: The word shime-daiko comes from the longer term tsukeshime-daiko, and the instrument is often shortened to shime-daiko, or simply shime. The prefix tsukeshime combines the Japanese verbs tsukeru (to fix, to attach) and shimeru (to bind tight, to fasten), and the compound suggests a tight, firm binding. Its naming reflects the instrument's central feature: the drumheads are joined to the body in a tight, fixed way. This construction lets the shime-daiko produce its distinctive, clear tone, which is why it is used so widely both in traditional Japanese music and in contemporary performance.

The drum sounds when the head is struck with a stick, and the higher the tension the more clearly the pitch rises above that of an ordinary taiko. 締太鼓是日本小型膜鳴樂器，短而寬的鼓身上下張動物皮鼓面；皮先固定在金屬箍上，再張: The shime-daiko is a small Japanese membranophone: animal-skin heads are stretched over the top and bottom of a short, wide body; the skins are first fixed to metal hoops and then drawn over the body, and the two heads are bound to each other with ropes. It is hung on a stand and struck with a stick, and because the heads are tightly stretched the pitch is relatively high. It is used in Japanese ensemble settings such as nagauta, hayashi, taiko ensemble and folk song, and has appeared in Japanese musical genres since mediaeval dengaku.
締太鼓音色清脆明亮，具有穿透力強的特質，能在樂隊中凸顯出來。其音域位於中高音區，: The shime-daiko has a clear, bright tone that carries strongly, so it stands out in an ensemble. Its range lies in the upper middle register, and its volume varies widely, from a soft tap to a ringing stroke. The tension of the head decides how bright or dark the tone is: tight and it is sharp and exciting, slack and it is gentler. Its resonance is distinctive, and the two-head design gives the sound layers, since the upper and lower heads can produce different timbres. Compared with the deep, heavy odaiko, the shime-daiko is light and nimble; compared with the Western snare drum, its tone has more of the cleanness and woodiness of Japanese tradition, combining a metallic brightness with the warmth of a traditional instrument.
締太鼓鼓身多採用桶狀木製結構，通常選用堅硬且音響特性良好的木材如樫木或松木製作。: The body is usually a barrel-shaped wooden construction, generally of a hard wood with good acoustic properties, such as oak or pine. The two heads are animal skin, traditionally horsehide or cowhide, treated to increase durability and tone quality. The heads are fixed tightly to the wooden body by metal hoops, the metal parts being made of copper or iron. The ropes are usually hemp or synthetic fibre, and are used to adjust the tension of the heads and so control the timbre.
